details: Samsung's annual Galaxy Unpacked event in July is expected to unveil new foldable devices, including the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Flip 8. These launches are a major highlight of the tech calendar, drawing significant attention.

While the Galaxy Z Fold 7 was noted for its slim profile, the Z Fold 8 is rumored to introduce a significant design change. There have been ongoing discussions about a shift to a shorter and wider form factor.
Today's leak from Android Headlines provides new renders of both the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Flip 8. These visuals offer a clearer look at the devices ahead of their anticipated debut.

The renders also showcase various color options and a range of accessories that will likely be available. Samsung typically offers a wide assortment of cases and other add-ons for its flagship launches.
Despite their high price tags, Samsung's Z Fold and Z Flip devices are among the year's biggest phone launches. Consumers are keenly awaiting improvements in durability and battery life.
The brand has continuously refined its foldable offerings. With the supposed launch roughly a month away, anticipation is high for Samsung to deliver compelling new models.

headline_marked: [[Base44 launches its own AI model]] Base1, trained on millions of user interactions, for app creation
headline: Base44 launches its own AI model Base1, trained on millions of user interactions, for app creation
summary: The move aims to boost defensibility, optimize latency and cost, and provide specialized performance for its vibe coding platform users.
details: Base44, the vibe coding platform acquired by Wix for $80 million, has begun rolling out its proprietary AI model, Base1. This model is designed to assist users in creating applications using natural language, marking a significant strategic shift for the company.

This development addresses a growing debate in the AI industry regarding the long-term defensibility of businesses built solely on third-party frontier models. Base44 aims to gain a competitive edge by owning and optimizing its core AI technology.

According to founder Maor Shlomo, training and owning their model allows for greater optimization in latency, cost, and efficiency compared to relying on general-purpose frontier models. This specialization is expected to deliver better results for their specific user base.

Base1 was developed and trained using a unique dataset generated from "tens of millions of real user interactions" on the Base44 platform. This extensive, proprietary data is key to the model's specialized performance and ongoing improvement.

The company faces competition from other vibe-coding platforms like Lovable, which uses external LLMs, as well as frontier AI labs such as xAI (Grok's parent company) and Anthropic's Claude Code, which are increasingly entering the app creation space.

Industry experts, like Jonathan Userovici of Headline VC, emphasize that data, distribution, and a strong tech stack are crucial for AI startup defensibility. Base44's strategy aligns with this by leveraging its unique data and infrastructure.

Cost reduction is a significant driver, as enterprise customers are increasingly demanding better ROI from AI solutions, leading to a need for optimized model selection. Base44 anticipates that owning Base1 will result in a structurally stronger margin profile over time.

Despite recent layoffs at its parent company Wix, Base44 has continued to grow its headcount since its acquisition and recently surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, demonstrating strong performance and market traction.
